title: Machine learning in point-of-care testing: innovations, challenges, and opportunities
abstract: The landscape of diagnostic testing is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into decentralized, rapid, and accessible sensor platforms for point-of-care testing (POCT). The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the shift from centralized laboratory testing but also catalyzed the development of next-generation POCT platforms that leverage ML to enhance the accuracy, sensitivity, and overall efficiency of point-of-care sensors. This Perspective explores how ML is being embedded into various POCT modalities, including lateral flow assays, vertical flow assays, nucleic acid amplification tests, and imaging-based sensors, illustrating their impact through different applications. We also discuss several challenges, such as regulatory hurdles, reliability, and privacy concerns, that must be overcome for the widespread adoption of ML-enhanced POCT in clinical settings and provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of ML-driven POCT technologies, highlighting their potential impact in the future of healthcare. Recent years have seen an increasing shift from centralized laboratory diagnostics to decentralized point-of-care testing, a shift which has the potential to increase health equity. Here the authors provide their perspective on how the integration of machine learning and artificial intelligence with point-of-care technologies can - and could - support this transition

claims.text: Applying machine learning models to HIV lateral flow assay image interpretation increased diagnostic specificity by 11% compared to visual interpretation by healthcare workers.
Applying machine learning models to HIV lateral flow assay image interpretation increased diagnostic sensitivity by 2.8% compared to visual interpretation by healthcare workers.
The SMARTAI-LFA platform achieved 98% sensitivity and 100% specificity for COVID-19 antigen detection.
The TIMESAVER deep learning system reduced lateral flow assay time to 1–2 minutes compared to the traditional 15 minutes.
An SVM classifier for magnetic nanoparticle-labeled lateral flow assays achieved 100% accuracy at an hCG concentration of 0.25 mIU/mL compared to 7% accuracy for visual reading.
Gold-ion amplified high-sensitivity vertical flow assays (hs-VFA) combined with neural network processing achieved a limit of detection of 0.2 pg/mL for cardiac troponin I.
A peptide-panel multiplexed vertical flow assay (xVFA) for Lyme disease achieved 95.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity.
Real-time fluorescent signal analysis with recurrent neural networks reduced the assay time of nucleic acid amplification tests by 45%.

Time-lapse coherent holographic imaging combined with deep learning detected live bacteria colonies within 9 hours, shortening detection time by over 12 hours compared to standard EPA-approved methods.

limitations.text: For cTnI in magnetic nanoparticle-labeled LFA, the quantification cut-off was limited to 0.5 ng/mL, falling short of the ~0.01 ng/mL sensitivity required for clinical use.

The performance of several microfluidic paper-based analytical device (µPAD) platforms was primarily demonstrated on synthetic and spiked samples, requiring further validation on biological specimens.
Subjective interpretation of POCT results by untrained users, such as reading faint test lines on rapid tests, causes significant diagnostic variability.
Traditional centralized laboratory testing faces limitations including lengthy turnaround times, high operational costs, and limited geographical accessibility.

future_work.text: Conduct systematic benchmarking and meta-analyses comparing machine learning algorithm performance across standardized multi-platform POCT datasets.
Develop explainable AI (XAI) frameworks tailored for point-of-care diagnostics to provide transparent feature attributions to clinicians.

Establish adaptive regulatory pathways (such as Software as a Medical Device pre-specifications and algorithm change protocols) integrated with real-world evidence for continuous AI postmarket oversight.

methodologies.name: SMARTAI-LFA Platform
methodologies.description: A deep learning-assisted smartphone lateral flow assay system that uses YOLOv3 for automated object detection of test regions and ResNet-18 for result classification.
datasets: COVID-19 swab and saliva clinical samples

methodologies.name: TIMESAVER-LFA Framework
methodologies.description: An immunoassay verification methodology using a combination of convolutional neural networks and time-series deep learning models to predict test results in 1–2 minutes.

methodologies.name: Multiplexed Vertical Flow Assay (xVFA) with Deep Learning
methodologies.description: A paper platform featuring vertical liquid flow across stacked layers with multi-spot reaction membranes, combined with fully connected neural networks for multiplexed biomarker quantification.
